subject.title: [Feature]: Improve `openclaw config` to avoid secrets and invalid files

question: Should bare interactive `openclaw config` change from the documented configure wizard to help output, and should literal writes to known secret config paths warn or fail in favor of SecretRefs?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses documented CLI compatibility and credential-safety policy, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Add narrow guardrails
options.body: Show help for bare `openclaw config` on already configured systems while preserving explicit `openclaw configure` and `--section`, and warn or fail only for registry-known secret literal writes with a clear SecretRef path.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Leave bare `openclaw config` as the wizard and rely on validate, SecretRef builders, redaction, and placeholder restoration for safer usage.

options.title: Go strict SecretRef-first
options.body: Fail closed for literal writes to supported secret targets, accepting a stronger security posture and higher upgrade/script compatibility impact.

recommendation.title: Add narrow guardrails
recommendation.body: Show help for bare `openclaw config` on already configured systems while preserving explicit `openclaw configure` and `--section`, and warn or fail only for registry-known secret literal writes with a clear SecretRef path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the shared config/configure CLI history and already provided prior maintainer-facing review on this unresolved issue.
